items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: but there was Feber there, we had Charley, Tom Whaley, we had Louis Jones. And there was a Bill Byrd, Sergeant Thorpe.

ctx.x: Yeah, we went to war. We went to, we landed in St. Nazare. We was -- when we came back to St. Nazare, we were deloused there. But it was a wonderful experience. When we came to America from there, we came in at Hampton Road, and the guys actually cried on each other's shoulders. We had some great guys in our band. A lot of them are

dead now, but there was Feber there, we had Charley, Tom Whaley, we had Louis Jones. And there was a Bill Byrd, Sergeant Thorpe. In fact, it was a great collection of mostly all New York musicians. I was about the only one that came from New Jersey. I tried three times before I got in that band, you know? That was the last band that was going over that wouldn't be a labor battalion, as far as the blacks were concerned, see?

So, I tried three times, and the last time I -- the second time, I was up there a lieutenant asked me, he said, "Hey young man, what do you want to do? Do you want to get shot? You'll get shot right here. Why you going over there?" Well, I said I wanted to get into the band. Well I got into the band, see, and I played baritone horn in there. I started out with the alto and then I went to the baritone. That's as far as I got, because I didn't want to -- I wanted to be in there to learn the art of music, which I…
